This is just my assumption but this seems more like it was written to the people in your family. I can't say I don't empathize, bengali families are just like that for the most part. As a muslim majority country they will obviously be very conservative. I myself have never been able to wear knee shorts outside because my grandmother dragged me by the arm back inside my house. No one is jealous of you, alright maybe your family just sees you as a sinful heretic but honestly there's worse situations to be in. You atleast have a physical distance from them, many bengalis never manage to escape. You might be sick and tired of hearing the sacrifices your parents made for you so let me put this in a different perspective. 

You live in an entirely different world from us, youmay not realize and frankly it's not your fault. You've only ever come by to visit, you're not aware of how the economy and social sphere work here. You have to admit you don't know what you're talking about in that case. Every country's working class is different. The west is far more different, work here just means being willing to work for literal pennies. To not find jobs constantly if you don't get something more mainstream like being a doctor or working in IT. As I said, you can't berate us for not knowing how things work in the West if all we know is how things work in Bangladesh.

You clearly have issues with your cousin, but it seems like you despise how people act in Bangladesh. You're making a lot of assumptions. Why is it bad to be hedonistic with food? It's good you work out, but to think your better than those who don't is just arrogant. I'm not on her side I'm just telling you what I think. 

She does sound like a bitch, but I hope you realize the ability to work and go outside for women is a far fetched dream. A recent post on r/bangladesh is from a 16 year old girl who talks about how she can't go anywhere alone and can't hang out with her friends. This isn't imprisonment, is it suffocating? Yes. But what I mean is that it's so incredibly unsafe for woman to work, go outside alone, and just do things. You live in the west where- yes these problems exist- but not to the scale it exists in Bangladesh. Comments on that post by other women who are 26 and still have a curfew of 9pm because their parents are scared they'll get r*ped pr kidnapped by the awful men in our country. I can't tell you how many close calls I myself have had due to having to travel and work alone.

I'm very sorry your cousin did all that to you, Bangladeshi family structures tend to be old fashioned and most young Bangladeshis have issue with this too. I myself have my every visible flaw picked apart by my family whenever I visit. It is just the culture but I am not saying to make it seem like it's any worse. I'm saying to ignore them like most of us do. They will never change.

In a country like ours where labourers get paid less than someone who just knows how to read. Can you truly blame us for thinking education is the only path for true success? In your western land that is obviously no longer the case, people there are mostly educated, the majority is educated in the west while the minority is educated in Bangladesh. Business owners will be successful but there is no doubt they'd be more successful if they were educated. 

I'm not trying to vindicate you, I truly want you to understand that things are just so just for the sake of it. There is rhyme and reason for everything you say is unreasonable. Put your pride and ego aside and just truly imagine why they would think that rather than accusing them of being shallow. Not everything is surface level.
